title: 32 Sources, One Queue: I Stopped Checking Feeds by Hand | vitalii.no
description:
How 6 Telegram channels and 26 RSS feeds became a single moderation queue that I check once instead of thirty-two times.

Every morning meant opening 6 Telegram channels and 26 RSS feeds, each with its own format and its own update rhythm, just to find out whether anything worth publishing had appeared. Thirty-two places to look. The checking itself was eating the hours meant for building.

GitHub Actions now does the rounds. realtime-scraper.yml runs every 10 minutes and works through the Telegram channels round-robin, one at a time, so the Bot API's rate limits are never touched. rss-monitor-v2.yml runs every 30 minutes and batches the 26 feeds eight at a time, which keeps each run inside the free Actions minutes instead of burning them. Everything lands in Supabase Edge Functions for scoring and dedup, and whatever survives arrives in one Telegram queue.

Thirty-two sources, one place to look. The round-robin has held the rate limits since it went in, and batching keeps the whole thing inside the free tier.
